source.title: DeRes: Decoupling Residual Stability and Adaptivity for Scalable CTR Prediction
source.authors: Wenzhuo Cheng; Shipeng Nie; Qixin Guo; Xuefeng Sun; Jianguo Lou; Zhengwei Zheng

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the venue and DOI contain placeholders.
record.tranche_reason: Uses power-law fitting as an analysis method for CTR models, but does not test the claim about language-model pretraining loss or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper fits CTR test AUC against FLOPs and reports results for three architectures. Those are related scaling results, but AUC on CTR models is not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy. The reported scaling-fit rows are therefore recorded under fits_no_version. Other CTR benchmark and ablation results do not measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper uses an AUC-versus-FLOPs power-law fit as a tool to compare its CTR architecture (DeRes-P) against baselines. The outcome is CTR test AUC over about one order of magnitude of per-sample FLOPs on one dataset. It is not held-out pretraining loss, and it is not a test of any claim version, including V5, which concerns the loss power-law form in other regimes. The fit serves mainly to show the authors' own method scales more steeply.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that DeRes beats twelve baselines by up to +0.32% AUC at under 5% extra FLOPs. They also report a steeper AUC–FLOPs scaling exponent (0.118 vs 0.071 for OneTrans), so an 8-layer DeRes matches a 16-layer OneTrans. Ablations support the dual-path, identity residual and SiLU choices.
record.recipe_differences: The paper fits test AUC versus per-sample FLOPs for CTR architectures, varying depth and width; it does not fit language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute, or optimize parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted exponent differs by architecture (OneTrans, DenseFormer, DeRes-P). The fit varies depth and hidden dimension; no sensitivity to language-model loss fitting choices is tested.

fits_no_version.finding: On the Industrial CTR dataset, test AUC versus per-sample FLOPs (0.3G–4.2G) is fit by AUC = α − β·C^−γ. The fitted γ is 0.071 for OneTrans, 0.089 for DenseFormer and 0.118 for DeRes-P.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CTR model AUC follows a saturating power law in per-sample FLOPs, with an exponent that depends on the inter-layer connection architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: In a depth sweep, OneTrans AUC gains only 0.09 pp from L=8 to L=16, while DeRes-P's gain over OneTrans rises with depth (+0.27 to +0.54 pp).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth scaling of standard-residual CTR Transformers saturates early, while cross-layer attention residuals sustain gains.

record.problems: The scaling fit covers one Industrial CTR dataset and five depth values with two hidden dimensions; the reported exponent uncertainty is not stated. The metric is CTR AUC rather than language-model pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were identified. CTR benchmark results and ablations in Sections 4.2–4.5 were left out because they do not measure the language-model loss, extrapolation, allocation, or downstream-behavior versions.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation of small-run loss fits to much larger runs.
Effect of depth/width on LM loss at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form of pretraining loss in other modalities or regimes. Only CTR AUC vs FLOPs over about 1 order of magnitude is reported.
Downstream LM task performance versus scale or loss.
Dependence of LM loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting or setup choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4/uses_without_test classification is retained. The scaling fit spans one dataset and about 14x compute, with no exponent uncertainty reported. Its functional form is a saturating AUC law, not a loss power law.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from small-run loss fits.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Language-model pretraining loss comparisons isolating architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Power-law pretraining-loss results in other modalities or training regimes; the paper reports CTR AUC, not pretraining loss.
Downstream language-model task performance related to scale or pretraining loss.
Sensitivity or disagreement in language-model loss exponents or compute-optimal splits due to fitting choices or setup.
